content: Where can see my public info

1. Open your web browser on the desktop where Savvy is running locally for you.
2. In the address bar, type `https://yourdomain.com/HR`. This will take you to the HR section of Oracle Fusion Cloud's Human Capital Management module within their system if public information sharing options are enabled and configured correctly.
3. Once on the HR page, look for tabs or sections labeled 'Public Information', often found in dashboard interfaces. Clicking this should display areas where you can see your name as it appears to external users who have access permissions granted by the company's IT policy. 
4. Remember that public information typically does not include sensitive data like Social Security numbers, payroll details or personal contact info unless specifically shared for business reasons and with proper consents in line with privacy laws such as GDPR.
Show my absences

1. Open the Oracle Fusion HCM Cloud application on your desktop by accessing the link provided or using any bookmark if you have one saved for quick access in future scenarios as well.
2. Locate and click on "HR" to enter the Human Resources section of the platform, which is where absence records are managed.
3. Inside the HR module, find and select the tab labeled 'Employee Absences' or similar depending on your interface version for visual representation of absenteeism data across employees in real-time; you will see a list displayed herein to review all recorded instances by date range if applicable, as well as filtering options allowing refine searches based upon absence type (such as illness, vacation) and approval status.
4. Upon identifying the employee's name for whom we seek information about their absences from either a dropdown selection or search function within that module interface – let’s assume this is John Doe – click on his profile to view detailed individual data concerning specific leave requests, if any are recorded and pending action; alternatively navigate through Absence Records as follows:
5. Utilize the absence record management feature by identifying an 'Add New' or similar button often located at the top of a list or sidebar within this module – in case there is no prior entry for John Doe, he would need to file his first request here; conversely, if existing records exist:
   - Identify and select one such record directly associated with 'John Doe' from an auto-populated dropdown (or list), which displays all of the absence fields as provided in your data extract. In this case let’s choose a pending status to find unrecorded absences that might have occurred:
6. Review relevant details for each entry by examining AbsenceId, type, and duration – ensuring consistency with official records; verify dates align correctly (StartDate, EndDate) as well as any approval actions tied to the absence through 'ApprovalStatus' field which may indicate if it was approved or pending.
7. Should additional information be required regarding specific absences beyond what is displayed in this module interface – such a request can typically include details like verification of illness, supporting documentation for unplanned leave etc.; navigate to the appropriate form section within HCM Cloud often located near 'Employee Absence' or directly underne0wn from it.
8. Complete necessary fields on absence forms with accurate information and submit them through designated buttons – typically labeled as ‘Submit’ or equivalent, taking care not only for correctness of entries but also that no contradictions exist within the data set itself; this may involve contacting supervisors if required to authenticate details provided by employees.
9. Once submission is completed successfully without errors - log off from HCM Cloud application after closing all open tabs/windows as prompted either via a confirmation message or through clicking on 'Log Out' option at the corner of your screen; save any pertinent absence records information locally if necessary for future reference using platform’s provided data export functionalities.
10. Finally, ensure that appropriate follow-up actions are taken to address absences – such as approval requests being processed in due course by supervisors and department heads or unplanned leaves covered through workload redistribution among team members; this helps maintain harmony within the working environment while also catering for employee wellness needs.
11 End of process - Remember to regularly check back into HCM Cloud application whenever needed henceforth, keeping track over time-wise trends in absence patterns or significant changes related thereof due diligently adhering rules & regulations pertaining managing human resources effectively within corporate organizations while simultaneously ensuring fair treatment towards staff members’ personal matters concerning health/life situations.

Time & Attendance Management System in Oracle Fusion HCM - A Detailed Exploration from Employee Self-service to Global Employer Considerations, with Insights on Absence Reporting Mechanisms | Workforce Software Services Ltd (WSS) Limited - January 13, 2024
    In an increasingly globalized world where labor markets intersect and international laws come into play when managing employee absences across different jurisdictions – like those in the European Union post-2014’s regulation limiting workweeks to a maximum of 35 hours, or Australia mandating clear reasons for time off requests - navigating through an organization's Time & Attendance Management System is not merely about handling absence data. It becomes essential knowledge that touches on organizational hierarchy and employee empowerment in attendance tracking.
    Employees within a well-crafted Oracle Fusion HCM system often wield the autonomy to report their absences, marking entries with specific dates for leave or approving requests through functionalities like 'New Entry.' This interaction is not only about maintaining records but also understanding and adhering to diverse legal requirements.
    The absence reporting mechanism within Oracle Fusion HCM enables employees (often via self-service portals) to:
    1) Log time off with justifications, which could be tied into broader compliance issues related to labor laws across different jurisdictions – for instance, ensuring that the recorded leave meets France's 35-hour workweek maximum without exceeding it. This is pivotal because violations can lead to legal disputes and financial penalties under European Union regulations.
    2) Approve or disapprove of absence requests made by colleagues, providing them with a measure for managing time off within the team – reflective of their hierarchical structure in an organization which should be clear from navigation menus labeled 'My Team.' Empowering employees through this process not only improves transparency but also ensures adherence to policies like those seen in Australia, where reasons behind requests must always be documented.
    3) Notify managers or HR representatives of any discrepancies – a feedback mechanism that can act as early warning systems for potential compliance issues; it's essential if employees report absence-related concerns promptly to mitigate the risk of unpaid leave disputes in jurisdictions with stringent policies.
    4) Provide immediate, real-time insights on request approval status or updates concerning policy changes – especially relevant when an organization may have undergone modifications post a period like 12 weeks ago which might not yet be reflected within the absence reporting tool due to delays in system implementation of new policies.
    This navigation process is also essential for head HR managers who need to address these requests, as they can quickly identify issues or misalignments with labor laws and intervene where necessary before any potential problems escalate into more significant organizational concerns such as non-compliance fees or worker dissatisfaction.
    The absence reporting mechanism is instrumental not only in maintaining accurate attendance records but also ensuring a transparent communication channel between employees, managers, and HR representatives – ultimately fostering trust within the organization while navigating hierarchies effectively for team-specific management of absences. It's important to note that this absence reporting system does come with its own set of challenges:
    Silent Alert System Implications - Without an active alert or notification mechanism, employees might miss out on crucial updates related to their requests or the status thereof, possibly leading to a disconnect between management and staff. Especially in scenarios where no immediate feedback is provided after approval processes (or lack of it), this silence can result in anxiety among team members waiting for confirmation about pending time off decisions; if unpaid leave policies are updated or extended beyond the usual notification window, employees might end up unaware and potentially disadvantaged.
    Conversely, introducing a robust alert system that provides timely updates regarding approval statuses – even after significant delays (e.g., 12 weeks) since request submission - can ensure alignment with labor laws like those in France or Australia while maintaining transparency and trust within the HR processes; this also assists managers in keeping track of long-term absence patterns that might indicate broader systemic issues requiring strategic interventions.
    While crafting an employee manual, it is vital to emphasize how navigation menus labeled 'My Team' are not only about access but rather a representation of the empowered structure within teams – where members understand their rights and responsibilities concerning absence reporting procedures (tied back into regulatory compliance). This section should underscore that such tools aren’t just bureaucratic necessities; they enhance engagement, streamline operations with legal standards as per global requirements like EU regulations or Australian law – while being mindful of cultural and regional specificity in workforce management practices.
